name: Urdu alphabet (Nastaliq)
signature: Right-to-left words descend diagonally in calligraphic Nastaliq, with dense joins and carefully placed dots.
combination: Letters join right-to-left and change shape by position. Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq; the bundled Naskh font is currently a readable fallback while the course data records Nastaliq structure. Short vowels are normally omitted.
notes: Starter inventory for the first Urdu shared-spine lessons, grounded in Zer o Zabar. This canonical script-data file keeps Noto Naskh as its readable path-checking fallback; the book and Language Ladder presentation use the separately vendored Noto Nastaliq Urdu family. The B1 core (chapters 264-275) added six recognition-only rows, ث ڈ ذ ص ع غ, each with an empty stroke order until an Urdu-scoped source is verified; ژ and the standalone hamza ء are still absent, so the full letter inventory remains explicit next-track work.
